scope: Native SysML projection; not native or C refinement admission

projection.construction.invariant: Begin allocates an initialized shell with MEM_ALLOC_KEYS and strong values before any payload store. Every installed key/value remains scanned across construction safepoints. Commit is nonallocating and publishes final weak/index flags plus KEY_MOVED and NEED_REHASH together. Binary alloc! roots the shell before recursively decoding fields; unpublished failure retains normal Scheme root/exception custody.
projection.construction.benefit: Replace flags-zero construction windows in both real decoders; GC transports every installed reference before the final semantic index policy becomes visible
projection.construction.cost: One existing flags word, no new object field or allocation. Pending weak entries are retained strongly until commit or abandonment; partial construction adds key scanning proportional to installed/unused table extent. Native roundtrip and exception paths still require qualification.
projection.creation.invariant: test-fn=false selects C identity index; a Scheme test/hash selects persistent SCHEME_INDEX bit 128. Same existing flags word; never infer ownership from KEY_MOVED or weak-key bits.
projection.creation.benefit: Native layout records the semantic algorithm owner before collector sees a table
projection.creation.cost: One constructor flag decision; no extra table field or root word
projection.repair.route: mem.c scan -> process_gc_hash_tables -> repaired key/value references and owner dispatch
projection.repair.invariant: Collector transports references. Scheme hashes must be stable for unchanged semantic keys across GC. Clear only address-driven KEY_MOVED for Scheme indexes; preserve pre-existing NEED_REHASH. Never call Scheme from GC or replace its index with the C address hash.
projection.repair.benefit: Eliminate wrong C rehash and its full-table traversal for Scheme-owned indexes; avoid adding a first-reader mutation after ordinary GC
projection.repair.cost: One owner branch per reached GC table. Correctness depends on hash stability; arbitrary physical-address-dependent custom hashes are not qualified.
projection.identity.route: object-scanning.inc actual strong-key movement; weak-tables.inc reference repair; hash-table-api.inc pure lookup and writer-owned reconstruction
projection.identity.invariant: GC never permutes slots. Actual native key movement records KEY_MOVED; pure reads with this debt linearly search current references without clearing debt or writing slots. Set, delete and path-compressing union/find rebuild before mutation. Deserialization NEED_REHASH stays distinct. No eager/lazy collector-count policy remains.
projection.identity.benefit: Stable suspended traversal and shared pure reads; permanent symbols no longer force a speculative whole-table rebuild on every GC
projection.identity.cost: One before/after identity comparison per strong heap key; moving-key reads can cost O(n) until the next mutation. Writer rebuild remains O(n). No new table field, heap increase or callback to Scheme in GC. Concurrent/reentrant same-table mutation is not admitted
projection.traversal.route: _system.scm gc-hash-table-for-each/search/foldl -> visitor -> GC -> same physical cursor
projection.traversal.invariant: Reference relocation and weak removal preserve slot positions; a strong unchanged table visits each binding once despite visitor GC. Mutator layout writes require no active traversal. doc/gambit.txi table-for-each forbids same-table public access/mutation; this cut does not lift that public restriction. Private native read is separately read-only.
projection.traversal.benefit: Remove GC-induced duplicate/missing visits without allocating a traversal snapshot or global reader lock
projection.traversal.cost: Requires caller exclusivity and rooted table/key/value state; weak removals may legitimately remove unreachable bindings. No guarantee for unowned raw pointers, concurrent writers or unknown-stop recovery
projection.scheme.route: _system.scm table-access -> recorded test/hash -> existing resize/reinsert for explicit reconstruction debt
projection.scheme.invariant: Ordinary GC does not create Scheme rebuild debt for stable hashes. Deserialization NEED_REHASH still blocks direct indexed lookup until Scheme reconstructs. GC never executes user hash callbacks.
projection.scheme.benefit: Semantic key/index agreement and no extra Scheme O(n) rebuild after every collection
projection.scheme.cost: Existing explicit rebuild may allocate/call user hash. Same-table mutating reentrancy and simultaneous reconstruction are not proved by this cut.
projection.lifetime.route: gc-hash-table-resize flag retention; table-copy -> make-table-aux; serialize/deserialize flags
projection.lifetime.invariant: Ownership survives allocation, resize, copy and current-format roundtrip. Older serialized images without owner metadata and external raw flag writers remain unqualified.
projection.lifetime.benefit: Owner is a persistent native contract, not a GC-mode switch or an exception for GSC
projection.lifetime.cost: Additional serialization/FFI producer inventory and native tests required; no compatibility inference
projection.witness.route: new target gsc default heap -> full two-pass bootstrap -> compiled map/multishot/GC and hash-index-owner controls
projection.witness.invariant: Default profile, real new runtime, both Scheme and native indexes. Large-heap and flag-intervention diagnostics explain failure but cannot confer acceptance.
projection.witness.benefit: Check actual generator, runtime index ownership, collector and repeatable control consumers together
projection.witness.cost: Full native and source-refinement gates; first target link is insufficient
projection.qnt.premise: One existing finite model: two semantic keys, one reader, two addresses/layouts, native address debt distinct from deserialize debt. Retain eager-reorder and unchanged-address reorder histories which duplicate a visited key despite valid hashing. The same QNT models one installed construction slot, GC relocation before commit and the flags-zero lost-reference counterexample; it assumes an externally retained key, not arbitrary weak reachability. Semantic hash stability and no concurrent writer are assumptions; not a C pointer or liveness proof
projection.lean.premise: Conditional semantic transport, native rebuild, incompatible-algorithm counter-law and debt guard; not a C pointer or complete hasher proof; construction reuses the existing reference-transport premise and adds no duplicate Lean schedule
projection.native.premise: Same Modern C source workspace and existing Bazel profile, retained generation, interpreted and compiled traversal with symbols/moving/retained-weak keys, map multi-shot, W<R and unknown join. Bind observed recipes, source locks and archived outcomes rather than treating a planned recipe as passed evidence. Earlier duplicate-key and compile failures remain retained. This incremental cohort is not a newly executed full bootstrap or remote CI
projection.ownership.premise: Trace all active C-target constructors, copies, resizing, serialization and raw producers; old images, reentrant mutation and concurrent reconstruction remain open
